own_solution.law: At launch, set x = 0 and t = 0. The truck follows x = 15t and the car follows x = (1/2)(2)t². Their subsequent meeting occurs at t = 2v/a = 15 s.
assumptions: Positions, velocities and acceleration are measured in the road frame.
The car maintains its stated acceleration through the subsequent meeting.
The roadside motorbike does not interact with either vehicle.

T56E0.regime: Conditional on replacing constant acceleration throughout with acceleration at 2 m/s² until 21 m/s, followed by constant-speed motion.

T35DB.regime: The cap exceeds the uncapped catch-up speed of 30 m/s; all listed caps, 38, 46 and 58 m/s, satisfy this condition.

T5651.regime: Conditional on replacing constant acceleration throughout with acceleration at 2 m/s² until 21 m/s, followed by constant-speed motion.

T76A7.regime: The cap exceeds the uncapped catch-up speed of 30 m/s; all listed caps, 38, 46 and 58 m/s, satisfy this condition.

TE8F1.regime: Conditional on interpreting the stated 2 m/s² as the acceleration before the kit's contribution.

TEA52.regime: Conditional on interpreting the stated 2 m/s² as the acceleration before the kit's contribution.

defect_reasons.contradictory_distractor_statement: T56E0 and T5651 impose a speed cap reached before catch-up, contradicting the stated constant acceleration unless that acceleration law is explicitly qualified.
defect_reasons.missing_assumption: TE8F1 and TEA52 do not establish whether the stated running acceleration of 2 m/s² excludes or already includes the kit's contribution, so the certified modified answers require an unstated interpretation.
defect_reasons.other: The authors' first assumption incorrectly says the initially stationary car passes the truck at launch, whereas the problem states that the moving truck passes the stationary car.

counterexamples: With the stated constant acceleration, the car reaches 21 m/s at 10.5 s, when it is still 47.25 m behind the truck; maintaining that acceleration until catch-up violates the added cap.
Under the authors' alternative acceleration-then-cruise model, caps of 17 and 21 m/s give 36.125 and 18.375 s respectively, but this model changes the problem's constant-acceleration condition.

For TE8F1, a kit fitted before launch can increase an untuned acceleration of 0.7 m/s² by 1.3 m/s², producing the explicitly stated running acceleration of 2 m/s² and a catch-up time of 15 s; interpreting 2 m/s² as the untuned acceleration instead gives 9.090909 s.
notes: The pass-1 substantive findings stand. The base relation and answer are correct. For the intended acceleration-then-cruise model, t = q²/[2a(q-v)] is dimensionally correct and gives both certified cap answers. The K predicate correctly places every listed cap above the uncapped catch-up speed of 30 m/s. For the intended additive-acceleration interpretation, t = 30/(2+q) gives 11.5384615, 9.0909091 and 6.6666667 s, agreeing with all displayed answers within rounding. These conditional calculations do not resolve the rendering defects. The disconnected assignments and their certified answers hold. Both declared minimal pairs retain the same numerical value and unit and change the intended attachment. The packet explicitly identifies the numeral-free controls as intentional, resolving the pass-1 observation about their absent numbers without creating a minimal-pair defect.
